findings.observed: `aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]` will be destroyed because its for_each key changed, and `aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]` will be created with the same `name` ("fixture-lifecycle-orders"). Terraform does not know they are the same object. The SQS queue would be destroyed with it, losing every message still in the queue.
findings.recommendation: Add a moved block (`from = aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]`, `to = aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]`) so Terraform changes the address in state instead. Applying as planned also tries to create a resource with the same name, which fails for globally named resources.
findings.title: `aws_sqs_queue.work["orders"]` is renamed to `aws_sqs_queue.work["order_events"]` without a moved block, so it will be destroyed and recreated

findings.observed: The IAM role is replaced because `name` ("fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v1" → "fixture-lifecycle-deploy-v2") cannot be changed in place. The new object is created before the old one is destroyed (create_before_destroy).
findings.recommendation: Check that the identifiers other systems hold for this resource (ARN, ID, DNS name, IP) are not referenced outside Terraform, or plan a cutover.
findings.title: `aws_iam_role.deploy` will be destroyed and recreated
